# p10k-rs v0.1.8 — DRAFT

> Status: **draft** — pending Sean's review. Replace this banner
> and tag when ready. The release workflow fires on
> `git push origin v0.1.8`.

**The "daemon health + unique-dir + AI statusline contracts" release.**
Slice 64 closes ADR-0001 § Follow-ups by adding a per-shell
daemon-respawn channel so a wedged or crashed `gitstatusd` no
longer forces every subsequent prompt onto the slow `ShellOut`
fallback for the rest of the shell's life. The ShellOut backend
itself catches up to `GixBackend` on per-category status counts.
The three AI hosts that have no public render-time protocol —
`cursor`, `aider`, `goose` — get pinned-empty contracts with test
guards so they can flip on additively when upstream protocols
exist. And `unique-dir` transient mode stops aliasing to
`same-dir` and ships a history-aware collapse approximation.

**Test count:** 603 passing, 3 ignored (559 at v0.1.7).
**Slice count:** 12 code commits + 4 docs commits since v0.1.7.
**Theme:** "daemon health hardening + AI host contracts +
unique-dir history."

## What you'll notice (visible changes)

### Daemon auto-respawn on wedge or crash

Before v0.1.8, a `gitstatusd` daemon that died (OOM-killed,
segfault, parent-zsh inheritance bug) or wedged (deadlock on a
pathological repo, FIFO read timeout) silently fell through to
the `ShellOut` backend for every subsequent prompt — typically
~25× slower. Recovery required restarting the shell.

The slice-64 daemon-respawn channel adds a `kill -0 $pid` probe
(~1ms cost) to a new `precmd` hook that runs **before** the
prompt-render `precmd`. A dead daemon triggers
`_p10k_rs_stop_daemon` + `_p10k_rs_start_daemon`; a wedge
sentinel (touched by the Rust client on a FIFO read timeout)
triggers the same respawn path. A new diagnostic subcommand
makes the state inspectable from any shell:

```sh
$ p10k-rs daemon-health
OK pid=12345 wedge=none
```

Five outcomes with stable exit codes for shell-script branching:

| Outcome | Stdout | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Healthy | `OK pid=<n> wedge=none` | 0 |
| Wedged | `WEDGED pid=<n> wedge_age_ms=<n>` | 2 |
| Dead | `DEAD pid=<n>` | 3 |
| Channel not wired | `NOT_WIRED` | 4 |
| I/O error | `ERROR <reason>` | 5 |

The full reference lives at `docs/src/reference/daemon-health.md`.

### `unique-dir` transient prompt actually does something now

Pre-v0.1.8, `transient_prompt = "unique-dir"` aliased to
`"same-dir"` — a documented stub since T1.8 landed in v0.1.4.
v0.1.8 ships a history-aware approximation:

```
seen_cwds = { current_cwd } ∪ history
collapse iff last_prompt_cwd ∈ seen_cwds
```

Where `history` is a NUL-separated file of cwds for all prompts
strictly older than the immediate previous prompt, maintained by
the zsh init inside the slice-9 mktemp dir (0700 perms,
auto-cleaned at shell exit). The Rust parser caps history at the
most-recent 64 entries on read so the file can grow per-prompt
without affecting decision latency.

This collapses strictly more prompts than `same-dir` (every
same-dir match plus every revisit to a previously-seen dir)
without ever incorrectly collapsing a prompt at a truly-unique
cwd. The strict upstream-p10k semantic ("collapse all but the
most recent prompt at each unique directory" via per-prompt-line-
position scrollback rewriting) remains deferred — that needs ZLE
machinery that addresses arbitrary prior prompts in scrollback,
not just the immediately-prior one.

### ShellOut per-category status counts

The `ShellOut` git backend's `git status --porcelain=v1 -z`
parser now populates `staged` / `unstaged` / `untracked` /
`has_conflicts` instead of the previous `dirty: bool`-only
coverage. Reaches `GixBackend` parity on the count axis; the
slice-60 phase-6 cross-check tests now compare all four buckets
backend-against-backend on the same repo state.

### Goose AI host segment renders

A trivial-looking bug — `HostKind::Goose` was detected by
`p10k-rs-ai` but `ai_host`'s `label()` match had no `Goose` arm,
so the wildcard hid the segment from the prompt even when Goose
was correctly identified. Now renders the `goose` label
alongside `claude-code` / `aider` / `cursor`.

### Per-host AI statusline contracts pinned

`cursor`, `aider`, and `goose` continue to return `""` from
`render_statusline` — none of them publish a render-time
protocol the way Claude Code does. v0.1.8 pins those empty
returns with test guards and research notes so flipping the
contracts on later is "pure additive" — no behavior change for
users, but the maintainer can't accidentally regress an
implementation that doesn't yet exist.

## Security posture (no surface changes)

- **No new third-party dependencies.** `Cargo.lock` diff since
  v0.1.7 is workspace-version-bumps only. `cargo deny check`:
  advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok.
- **`unique-dir` history file inherits slice-9 perms.** The
  file lives inside `$_P10K_RS_FIFO_DIR` (`mktemp -d` with
  `chmod 0700`) so only the owning UID can read it. The Rust
  parser does byte-level NUL split + direct `PathBuf::from(OsStr)`
  for equality compare only — no canonicalization, no symlink
  resolution into render-path text. Torn writes (race between
  precmd append and zle-line-finish read) fall back to empty
  history silently; the prompt never panics over a transient
  signal.
- **Daemon-respawn channel hardening.** PID file is written
  0600 inside a `umask 077` subshell; wedge sentinel inherits
  the 0700 dir; `kill -0 $pid` is a probe (cannot signal). The
  `_P10K_RS_GITSTATUSD_PID_FILE` and `_P10K_RS_GITSTATUSD_WEDGE`
  env vars are explicitly unset by `_p10k_rs_stop_daemon` so a
  failed respawn can't leave a stale path pointing at a deleted
  file.
- **No `unsafe` added.** The `unsafe` budget stays in
  `p10k-rs-git` for the gitstatusd FIFO open path; nothing new
  in v0.1.8 touches it.

## Upgrading

```sh
git pull
./install.sh
```

No config-file migration needed. Existing `transient_prompt =
"unique-dir"` configs change behavior on this version
(approximation replaces the same-dir alias) — if the new
behavior isn't wanted, revert to `transient_prompt = "same-dir"`.
